bibliographic.title: Large Language Models and Empathy: Systematic Review
bibliographic.authors: Vera Sorin; Dana Brin; Yiftach Barash; Eli Konen; Alexander Charney; Girish Nadkarni; Eyal Klang
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sorin, V., Brin, D., Barash, Y., Konen, E., Charney, A., Nadkarni, G., & Klang, E. (2024). Large language models and empathy: Systematic review. Journal of Medical Internet Research. https://doi.org/10.2196/52597

methodology.sample_description: English-language full-length publications evaluating empathy in LLM outputs; 12 studies published in 2023 included after database and reference searching
methodology.technology_context: ChatGPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA, and fine-tuned chatbots evaluated for empathy-related outputs in medical and other contexts

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article systematically reviews LLM empathy capacity and evaluation metrics; the provided text contains no focus on conversational governance, accountability, oversight, audit, compliance, guardrails, or operational risk controls.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the study is LLM-specific, conversational (chatbots, patient questions), and healthcare-regulated, its objective and synthesis center on empathy performance rather than governance mechanisms. Python triage flagged borderline status with governance_accountability score 1/3 and risk_audit_compliance 0/3, consistent with exclusion for the conversational governance review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Deterministic triage returned borderline_manual (76.0/100) with weak governance and zero risk/audit signals; manual confirmation needed because LLM, conversational, and healthcare dimensions scored highly.

appraisal.notes: As a systematic review on empathy, objectives, search strategy, inclusion criteria, and summarized limitations are reasonably clear in the provided excerpt. Full critical appraisal items (dual screening, risk-of-bias assessment of included studies, PRISMA reporting completeness) are not evidenced in the supplied text. Transferability to conversational governance is low because governance constructs are absent.

cerqual.explanation: For the target review on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems, this study offers low relevance despite moderate adequacy as an empathy-focused systematic review. The provided text does not supply governance-related findings, frameworks, or operational controls.

coding.theme: LLM empathy performance in healthcare and other contexts
coding.subtheme: evaluation of empathic chatbot and LLM responses

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs exhibit elements of cognitive empathy, recognizing emotions and providing emotionally supportive responses; ChatGPT-3.5 and other models were reported to perform well on empathy-related tasks, sometimes outperforming humans, but with noted limitations.
synthesis.contribution: Narrative systematic synthesis of 12 2023 studies on empathy in LLM outputs, summarizing models tested, evaluation metrics, and performance patterns in medical and other settings.
synthesis.limitations: Reported model limitations include repetitive empathic phrases, difficulty following instructions, overly lengthy responses, sensitivity to prompts, and reliance on subjective evaluation metrics influenced by evaluator background.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance; at most peripheral background on healthcare LLM/chatbot interaction quality, not governance, oversight, or compliance.

evidence.claim: Study is a systematic review of LLM empathy capacity
evidence.excerpt: We aimed to review the literature on the capacity of LLMs in demonstrating empathy.

evidence.claim: Includes chatbots and healthcare conversational context but not governance
evidence.excerpt: 6 studies comparing it with other LLMs such GPT-4, LLaMA (Meta), and fine-tuned chatbots. Seven studies focused on empathy within a medical context.

evidence.claim: Search methods and inclusion criteria are described
evidence.excerpt: We conducted a literature search on MEDLINE, Google Scholar, PsyArXiv, medRxiv, and arXiv between December 2022 and February 2024.

evidence.claim: Sample size of included primary studies
evidence.excerpt: A total of 12 studies published in 2023 met the inclusion criteria.
ChatGPT-3.5 (OpenAI) was evaluated in all studies, with 6 studies comparing it with other LLMs such GPT-4, LLaMA (Meta), and fine-tuned chatbots.
In health care, empathy is a fundamental for health care professionals and patients’ interaction.

evidence.claim: No governance, audit, or compliance focus in provided text
evidence.excerpt: Evaluation metric included automatic metrics such as Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation and Bilingual Evaluation Understudy, and human subjective evaluation.

Limitations were noted, including repetitive use of empathic phrases, difficulty following initial instructions, overly lengthy responses, sensitivity to prompts, and overall subjective evaluation metrics

evidence.claim: Main conclusion on empathy rather than governance
evidence.excerpt: Conclusions: LLMs exhibit elements of cognitive empathy, recognizing emotions and providing emotionally supportive responses in various contexts.
The search query was “((“large language models”) OR (llms) OR (gpt) OR (chatgpt)) AND ((empathy) OR (“emotional awareness”) OR (“emotional intelligence”) OR (emotion))
